raw_response:
Well, let me think this through. I'm getting on in years — 64 now — and it's just me and the wife at home. The kids are grown and working in town. So labor is the first thing on my mind when I plan the year.

I've been farming this 10.1 mu of cotton land for a long time. Cotton is what I know. I tried thinking about switching to wheat-maize a few years back when some of the neighbors did, but at my age the double-cropping turnaround is too much running around. Cotton I can handle at my own pace, and the price has been okay — not great, but okay. The county still has the cotton tradition out here on the western side.

**Planting.** I'll put the seed in around April 20th, give or take a few days depending on the soil temperature. I always check if the ground is warm enough — if I stick my hand in and it's still cold, I wait. Last year I planted on the 22nd and the stand came up fine. I buy the hybrid seed from the agricultural supply shop in town — the extension fellow recommends certain varieties and I go with what's been working. Costs me about 60 yuan per mu for seed these days, maybe a bit more. I don't save seed anymore, hybrid doesn't work that way.

**Tillage.** I'll plow once in the fall after picking is done, then harrow and make the ridges in spring before planting. I hire the tractor operator from the village — 50 yuan or so per mu for the plowing. I can't do it by hand at my age, and I don't own a tractor. That's just how it is.

**Fertilizer.** This is where I try to be careful with money. For cotton, I put down a compound fertilizer (the 15-15-15 kind) as a base before planting — about 40 kg per mu, that gives me roughly 6 kg N, 6 kg P, 6 kg K. Then at flowering and boll-setting I topdress with urea, maybe 15 kg of urea per mu, which adds about another 7 kg of N. So all together around 13 kg N per mu. The extension guy used to say you could push 18 or 20, but I've found that too much nitrogen makes the plant grow leafy and the bolls don't set as well. Cotton is picky that way. My neighbor down the road does about the same.

**Irrigation.** I have well access, but pumping costs money — electricity and the time. For cotton I usually irrigate twice: once after planting if it's dry to get the stand established, and once at flowering/boll-setting which is the critical time. If we get good rain in July I might skip the second one. Last year was dry so I watered three times and my electric bill hurt.

**Pesticide.** Cotton needs spraying, there's no way around it. Aphids early, then cotton bollworm in summer. I'll spray insecticide maybe 4-5 times through the season, and I use herbicide before planting to keep the weeds down. Fungicide only if I see something — usually I don't. I buy from the same supply shop, they know what works around here.

**Labor.** This is my biggest worry. Me and my wife can do most of the work — the spraying, the hoeing, the topdressing. But picking cotton is hard, bent over all day, and at 64 my back isn't what it was. I'll hire some help during picking season, probably 15-20 days of hired labor across 3-4 pickings. That's a real expense, maybe 100 yuan a day now, but I don't have a choice.

**Yield.** Last year I got about 250 kg of lint per mu. Year before was 270. I'm expecting around 250 this year if the weather is ordinary. I'm not going to chase high numbers at my age — steady is good.
